draft.answer: \((x^2-4)/(x-2)=x+2\) for \(x\ne2\). The original expression has domain \(\mathbb R\setminus\{2\}\). The simplified formula \(x+2\) is defined for every real number, so it is not equivalent to the original expression at every real number: at \(x=2\), the original is undefined whereas \(x+2=4\).

proof_steps.justification: x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2). On the domain from domain-check, x - 2 is nonzero, so it may be cancelled.
domain-check excludes x = 2 from the original expression. The polynomial x + 2 is defined at x = 2 and has value 4.
